node.statement: Let U in calU satisfy sigma(U)=U and ||U-J||<rho. Exact unitality gives phi_J(U)=U-J=:B; its anti-Hermitian and Hermitian parts A=B^parallel and B^perp each have norm at most ||B||, because dagger is isometric, so A lies in B_rho^{i calH}(0) and both parts lie in the domains from (A_2). Since U=J bold-dot (J+B) and U^dagger bold-dot U=J, the defining expression gives f_J(B)=0; uniqueness in (A_2) therefore yields B^perp=g_J(A), hence U=chi_+(A). The fixed-point equality and same-chart retention imply F_+(A)=phi_J^parallel(U)=A, so G_+(A)=0; 1.3 forces A=0, and uniqueness gives g_J(0)=0, whence U=J. Conversely J is fixed by 1.2, so J is the only fixed point in its ambient rho-ball.
